UseCaseIdentification.Name: Manual Frequency Restoration Reserve (mFRR) Provision by a Multi-Asset Prosumer Facility via VPP Aggregation
UseCaseIdentification.Zones: Process, Field, Station, Operation, Enterprise, Market

Scope.Paragraph: This use case covers the participation of an ePIPV facility (comprising BESS, EV charging infrastructure, PV generation, and non-flexible facility loads) in the mFRR balancing service market managed by the TSO. The facility offers both upward and downward regulation capacity through a VPP/Aggregator acting as BSP. It covers the day-ahead capacity assessment and procurement process, the real-time activation event triggered by the TSO through the balancing activation platform, and the coordinated multi-asset response executed by the Facility EMS. The use case is supported by four System Use Cases: SUC-PT-02.1 (mFRR Capacity Assessment and Optimisation), SUC-PT-02.2 (mFRR Market Bidding and Contract Management), SUC-PT-02.3 (Real-Time EMS Execution), and SUC-PT-02.4 (Settlement).

Objectives.Objective: Generate revenue for the ePIPV Site Owner by offering mFRR capacity to the TSO through the VPP/Aggregator, covering both capacity availability remuneration and energy activation remuneration. Demonstrate the technical capability of a mixed asset portfolio (BESS, EV charging, and PV) to deliver a coordinated frequency restoration response in both upward and downward regulation directions. Demonstrate that a multi-asset prosumer facility can reliably maintain asset readiness during contracted delivery periods and meet mandatory response time requirements upon activation.

ShortDescription.Paragraph: The ePIPV facility offers mFRR capacity to the TSO through a VPP/Aggregator registered as BSP. Day-ahead, the Facility EMS determines the available regulation capacity that can be committed for each 15-minute slot and communicates it to the VPP/Aggregator, which submits a capacity bid to the TSO's mFRR capacity market. If awarded, the facility stands ready to activate during the contracted delivery period. Upon receiving an activation signal from the TSO, the VPP/Aggregator forwards the order to the Facility EMS, which immediately coordinates the response across all available assets by modulating BESS, EV charging, and PV generation curtailment in the direction and magnitude required within the mandatory response time.

CompleteDescription.Paragraph: The ePIPV Site Owner operates a facility with a portfolio of assets capable of delivering power regulation in both directions. For upward regulation, the facility can discharge the BESS, reduce or pause EV charging sessions, and reduce or remove any existing PV generation curtailment, thereby increasing PV output and effectively reducing net consumption or increasing net injection. For downward regulation, the facility can charge the BESS at increased rate, raise EV charging power, and apply or increase PV generation curtailment, thereby decreasing PV output. The facility participates in the mFRR market through a VPP/Aggregator registered as BSP with the TSO, whose Offer Area encompasses the facility's assets aggregated within the VPP/Aggregator's BSP portfolio.

On the day before delivery (D-1), the Facility EMS assesses the available mFRR capacity for each 15-minute slot of the following day. This assessment takes into account forecast building load profiles, expected PV generation, projected BESS state-of-charge trajectory, and the probability distributions of EV availability derived from CPO historical data. For each slot and each regulation direction, the Facility EMS computes the maximum activatable power. This available capacity profile is communicated to the VPP/Aggregator, which aggregates it with capacity from other sites in its portfolio and submits a combined capacity bid to the TSO's mFRR capacity market before the relevant gate closure. The TSO evaluates submitted bids, clears the capacity market, and awards contracts for the delivery day. The VPP/Aggregator communicates the awarded capacity and contracted delivery periods back to the Facility EMS.

The Facility EMS uses the awarded schedule to determine which periods require readiness, and enters a state of readiness for those periods, maintaining the contracted assets within the bounds required to guarantee activatability, ensuring BESS state-of-charge is within the range needed to respond, and that scheduled EV departures do not conflict with the activation window. During the contracted delivery period, the TSO monitors system frequency and balance. If a balancing need arises, the TSO issues an activation order specifying direction, power magnitude, and duration. Activation orders can be of two types: scheduled activations, planned for a specific upcoming 15-minute slot and communicated to the BSP at least 10 minutes before delivery; and direct activations, issued immediately in response to unexpected unavailability of other balancing resources. In both cases, the order is transmitted through the balancing activation platform to the VPP/Aggregator, which immediately forwards it to the Facility EMS.

The Facility EMS executes the activation by coordinating the response across available assets: for upward regulation it prioritises BESS discharge, reduces or pauses EV charging sessions in progress, and removes any existing PV generation curtailment to increase PV output; for downward regulation it charges the BESS at increased rate, raises EV charging setpoints, and applies or increases PV generation curtailment to reduce PV output. The combination and sequencing of assets is determined by the Facility EMS to meet the required power and duration within the mandatory response time (a maximum 12.5-minute preparation period and a maximum 12.5-minute ramping period, per the standardised European mFRR product). The Facility EMS confirms activation to the VPP/Aggregator, which reports delivery to the TSO. Following the activation, the Facility EMS manages the recovery of each asset to its pre-activation or operationally preferred state, subject to any continuation instructions from the TSO.

At the end of the settlement period, the TSO aggregates activation records and delivery data, verifies the delivered activation against the contracted commitment, and computes the settlement, comprising a capacity remuneration for the contracted availability during the delivery period (EUR/MW/h), and an energy remuneration for the power actually delivered during any activation events (EUR/MWh). The VPP/Aggregator receives the settlement, acknowledges it, and allocates both components to the ePIPV Site Owner according to the aggregation agreement, which acknowledges receipt.

KPI.Name: Operation Cost (ePIPV)
KPI.Description: Reduction of the facility operating cost through mFRR capacity and activation remuneration and coordinated multi-asset operation. Target: reduce >=25% vs non-optimal

KPI.Name: Flexibility Participation (Operation)
KPI.Description: Increase of the flexibility the facility actually offers and delivers to the market, through contracted mFRR capacity and delivered activations. Target: increase >=100%

KPI.Name: Flexibility Potential
KPI.Description: Increase of the flexible power and energy capacity the facility can offer, by coordinating BESS, EV charging and PV curtailment. Target: increase >=25%

KPI.Name: Constraints Violation Occurrence
KPI.Description: Decrease of the occurrences of asset, grid-connection or EV-user constraint violations during mFRR readiness and activation periods. Target: decrease >=15%

Assumptions.Assumption: The ePIPV facility comprises PV generation, BESS, non-flexible commercial facility loads, and EV charging infrastructure, all monitored and controlled by a Facility EMS capable of adjusting the operation of each asset in real time.
The ePIPV facility has access to a VPP/Aggregator that aggregates the facility's flexibility capacity within a broader portfolio for mFRR market participation as BSP.

EV users accept that their charging sessions may be subject to modulation during contracted mFRR delivery periods within bounds that guarantee delivery of their minimum energy requirement by departure time.

The capacity offered to this market is determined jointly with the facility's other market commitments (day-ahead spot market participation via BUC-PT-01, DSO flexibility market via BUC-PT-03) within a single EMS optimisation run that maximises overall facility revenue across all available market channels.

mFRR Band capacity is contracted in Portugal through two parallel products: a monthly-maturity auction (operational since January 2024) and a newer daily-maturity auction introduced by ERSE in September 2025 specifically to enable storage and renewables participation. This BUC targets the daily mFRR Band product, consistent with the facility's BESS-centric flexibility profile.

Prerequisites.Prerequisite: The Facility EMS receives real-time data from all facility assets (PV generation, BESS state-of-charge, EV charging sessions, non-flexible load measurements).

Reliable bi-directional communication exists between the local Facility EMS, the VPP/Aggregator platform, and the TSO balancing activation platform, meeting the minimum availability requirements defined by the TSO.
A contractual aggregation agreement exists between the ePIPV Site Owner and the VPP / Aggregator BSP.
The VPP / Aggregator BSP holds a valid BSP registration with the TSO and its Offer Area has passed the TSO qualification test.

The EV charging infrastructure supports smart charging (dynamic power setpoint modulation via a charging management protocol), allowing the Facility EMS to adjust individual session charging rates in real time.

ClassificationInformation.RelationToOtherUseCases: This BUC's day-ahead capacity assessment (SUC-PT-02.1) shares a single EMS optimisation run with BUC-PT-01 (day-ahead spot market participation) and BUC-PT-03 (DSO flexibility market), which jointly determine how facility flexibility is allocated across market channels to maximise total revenue.
ClassificationInformation.LevelOfDepth: Business use case, detailed down to system use cases (SUC-PT-02.1 to SUC-PT-02.4) and their step-by-step sequences.
ClassificationInformation.Prioritisation: High. Demonstrates the provision of an ancillary service (mFRR) by a multi-asset prosumer facility, evaluated on both AC and DC infrastructure at the INESC-ID laboratory.
ClassificationInformation.GenericRegionalNationalRelation: The Portuguese pilot executes this BUC as a parallel comparison between AC infrastructure, tested as Hardware-in-the-Loop against a Digital Twin of the Continente facilities, and DC infrastructure, physically emulated as Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop at the INESC-ID laboratory. This comparison produces two infrastructure-level indicators, PT-KPI-01 (AC/DC Infrastructure Energy Efficiency) and PT-KPI-02 (DC vs AC Flexibility Capacity Advantage), which compare the two architectures rather than measure the objectives of this BUC. This methodology is specific to the Portuguese pilot's dual-infrastructure design and does not affect the BUC's applicability to a single-infrastructure deployment elsewhere.
ClassificationInformation.FurtherKeywords: mFRR, balancing services, VPP, aggregation, BESS, EV charging, PV curtailment, TSO.

GeneralRemarks.Paragraph: This BUC is evaluated at the INESC-ID laboratory, which has the capability of testing and emulating both AC and DC infrastructures, using a downscaled replica of the commercial facility. The ePIPV facility, comprising PV, BESS, EV charging and non-flexible commercial loads, is managed by a Facility EMS that assesses the available mFRR capacity day-ahead. A VPP / Aggregator BSP bids this capacity to the TSO and forwards activation orders received through the balancing activation platform. The features tested are the day-ahead capacity assessment and bidding, readiness maintenance, the coordinated multi-asset activation response, and settlement. The actors involved are the ePIPV Site Owner, the VPP / Aggregator BSP, the TSO, the Facility EMS and the Balancing Activation Platform.

ScenarioOverview.ScenarioDescription: The Facility EMS backend computes load, PV, EV availability, and BESS SoC trajectory forecasts and computes available mFRR capacity per 15-min slot and direction.
ScenarioOverview.PreCondition: Facility EMS has access to historical and real-time data required for forecasting
ScenarioOverview.PostCondition: A capacity profile (MW per slot, per direction) is ready for bidding

ScenarioOverview.ScenarioName: mFRR Market Bidding and Contract Management (SUC-PT-02.2)
ScenarioOverview.ScenarioDescription: The VPP / Aggregator BSP aggregates the facility's capacity into its portfolio, bids into the day-ahead mFRR capacity market, and the awarded contract is confirmed back to the Facility EMS.
ScenarioOverview.PreCondition: Capacity profile from SUC-PT-02.1 is available
ScenarioOverview.PostCondition: Contracted capacity and delivery periods confirmed at the Facility EMS

ScenarioOverview.ScenarioDescription: The Facility EMS loads the contracted schedule, maintains asset readiness through the contracted delivery period, and upon receiving an activation order executes a coordinated multi-asset response and reports delivery.
ScenarioOverview.TriggeringEvent: Start of contracted delivery period / TSO activation order
ScenarioOverview.PreCondition: Contracted capacity and delivery periods have been confirmed (SUC-PT-02.2)
ScenarioOverview.PostCondition: Activation delivered and confirmed; assets recovered to pre-activation state

ScenarioOverview.ScenarioDescription: The TSO verifies delivered activation against the contracted commitment and issues settlement; the VPP / Aggregator BSP allocates remuneration to the ePIPV Site Owner.
ScenarioOverview.PreCondition: Activation deliveries for the settlement period are confirmed and recorded
ScenarioOverview.PostCondition: Remuneration allocated to the ePIPV Site Owner

Step.DescriptionOfProcessActivity: Facility EMS backend computes building load forecast for the next 24h in 15-min slots.
Facility EMS backend computes PV generation forecast for the next 24h in 15-min slots, fed by a solar irradiance/production API.
Facility EMS backend computes EV arrival/departure probability distributions from historical CPO session data.
Facility EMS backend projects the BESS state-of-charge trajectory for the next 24h from the current SoC and the day's expected operating profile.
Facility EMS computes available mFRR capacity per 15-min slot, per direction, from the combined inputs.

Scenario.name: 4.2.2 mFRR Market Bidding and Contract Management (SUC-PT-02.2)

Step.DescriptionOfProcessActivity: Facility EMS communicates available capacity profile and activation constraints.
VPP / Aggregator BSP aggregates facility capacity with portfolio; submits combined capacity bid before gate closure.
TSO clears capacity market; communicates awarded capacity and contracted delivery periods.
VPP / Aggregator BSP forwards awarded capacity contract and contracted delivery periods.
Facility EMS receives the awarded capacity contract and contracted delivery periods (from SUC-PT-02.2) and determines which periods require readiness.
Facility EMS enters readiness state for the identified periods: manages BESS SoC within activation range, monitors EV departure schedules.
During the contracted delivery period, TSO issues an activation order specifying type, direction, power magnitude, and duration.
Balancing Activation Platform routes the activation order to the BSP.
VPP / Aggregator BSP forwards the activation order to the Facility EMS.

Facility EMS executes the response within the mandatory response time. Upward regulation: discharges BESS, reduces EV charging, removes PV curtailment. Downward regulation: charges BESS, increases EV charging rate, curtails PV.
Facility EMS confirms activation delivery: actual power delivered, assets mobilised, timestamps.
VPP / Aggregator BSP reports activation delivery.
Facility EMS manages asset recovery to pre-activation or operationally preferred state.
TSO aggregates activation records and delivery data for the settlement period.
TSO verifies delivered activation against the contracted commitment.
TSO computes capacity remuneration (EUR/MW/h) and energy remuneration (EUR/MWh).
TSO issues settlement to the VPP / Aggregator BSP.
VPP / Aggregator BSP acknowledges settlement receipt.
VPP / Aggregator BSP allocates remuneration to the ePIPV Site Owner per the aggregation agreement.
ePIPV Site Owner acknowledges receipt of remuneration.

Information.Name: Capacity availability profile
Information.Description: Time series per 15-min slot: available upward capacity (MW), available downward capacity (MW), activation constraints

Information.Name: mFRR capacity bid
Information.Description: Bid ID, direction (up/down), quantity (MW) per slot, price (EUR/MW/h), portfolio composition reference

Information.Name: mFRR capacity contract award
Information.Description: Contract ID, awarded capacity (MW) per slot/direction, contracted delivery periods (start/end timestamps), cleared capacity price (EUR/MW/h)

Information.Name: Activation order
Information.Description: Order ID, type (scheduled/direct), direction (up/down), power magnitude (MW), duration, mandatory response time

Information.Name: Activation delivery confirmation
Information.Description: Order ID reference, actual power delivered (MW) per timestep, assets mobilised (BESS/EV/PV), delivery timestamps

Information.Name: mFRR settlement result
Information.Description: Settlement period, capacity remuneration (EUR/MW/h), energy remuneration (EUR/MWh), total delivered energy (MWh)

Actor.Name: ePIPV Site Owner
Actor.Description: Entity that owns and operates the ePIPV facility and its distributed energy resources, and contractually delegates mFRR market participation to the VPP / Aggregator BSP

Actor.Name: VPP / Aggregator BSP
Actor.Description: Party that aggregates the facility's flexibility capacity within a broader portfolio, submits capacity bids to the TSO, forwards activation orders to the Facility EMS, reports delivery, and manages settlement

Actor.Name: TSO
Actor.Description: Party that procures mFRR capacity day-ahead, issues activation orders during contracted delivery periods, verifies delivered service, and issues settlement

Actor.Name: Facility EMS
Actor.Description: System that monitors and controls all facility assets, assesses available mFRR capacity day-ahead, maintains asset readiness during contracted periods, and executes the coordinated multi-asset activation response upon receiving an activation order

Actor.Name: Balancing Activation Platform
Actor.Description: Platform through which TSO activation orders are routed to BSPs

RequirementCategory.Name: Asset integration and commissioning
RequirementCategory.Description: All physical assets must be installed, commissioned, operational and addressable before pilot operation

Requirement.Name: Asset capability registration
Requirement.Description: The platform shall maintain the technical capabilities and operating limits of each asset, including rated power, energy capacity, control modes, ramp limits, SoC limits and availability.

Requirement.Name: Market asset registration
Requirement.Description: Assets intended for market or flexibility participation shall be registered with the required technical, metering, connection-point and geographic attributes before qualification or bidding.

RequirementCategory.Name: Energy Management System capabilities
RequirementCategory.Description: Contains requirements related to EMS functionalities and capabilities

Requirement.Name: Multi-asset orchestration
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall coordinate EV charging, PV generation, BESS operation, controllable loads and grid exchange within the applicable pilot boundary.

Requirement.Name: Schedule and setpoint generation
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall translate optimisation results and external commitments into asset-level schedules, limits and setpoints.

Requirement.Name: Constraint enforcement
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall prevent dispatch that violates grid connection limits, asset limits, user requirements, mobility-service constraints or contracted reserve obligations.

Requirement.Name: Flexibility estimation
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall calculate available upward and downward flexibility by time interval, including power, energy, duration and limiting constraints.

Requirement.Name: Distributed-site aggregation
Requirement.Description: The EMS or VPP layer shall aggregate multiple charging clusters or facilities into a single controllable and reportable portfolio without losing site-level constraints.

Requirement.Name: Operating-mode management
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall support normal, constrained-grid, market-activation, emergency and recovery modes with explicit transition rules.

RequirementCategory.Name: Smart charging, V2G and mobility-service constraints
RequirementCategory.Description: The charging infrastructure functionalities and capabilities

Requirement.Name: Dynamic charging control
Requirement.Description: The charging infrastructure shall accept remote time-based charging profiles or dynamic power limits for individual EVSEs or sessions.

RequirementCategory.Name: Communications and connectivity
RequirementCategory.Description: Collection of requirements to enable reliable communication

Requirement.Name: Bidirectional communications
Requirement.Description: Bidirectional communication shall be available wherever both telemetry and remote control are required between assets, EMS, CSMS, BMS, VPP and external platforms.

Requirement.Name: Message acknowledgement
Requirement.Description: Control commands and market activations shall be acknowledged by the receiving system with acceptance, rejection or failure status.

Requirement.Name: Store-and-forward capability
Requirement.Description: Where temporary loss of connectivity is possible, systems shall buffer non-real-time telemetry and forward it after reconnection without duplication.

Requirement.Name: External platform connectivity
Requirement.Description: The VPP/aggregator or EMS shall provide reliable interfaces to day-ahead, intraday, balancing and DSO flexibility platforms as applicable.

RequirementCategory.Name: Data acquisition, quality and storage
RequirementCategory.Description: Requirements for common data management mechanisms

Requirement.Name: Operational telemetry acquisition
Requirement.Description: The platform shall acquire EVSE, PV, BESS, meter, site-load, weather and mobility data required by the applicable use case.

Requirement.Name: Common timestamping
Requirement.Description: All operational records shall contain timestamps referenced to a common time base and include timezone or UTC information.

Requirement.Name: Data validation
Requirement.Description: Incoming data shall be checked for missing values, staleness, invalid ranges, inconsistent units and implausible changes before use in control or settlement.

Requirement.Name: Historical data retention
Requirement.Description: Historical measurements, schedules, commands, forecasts, user declarations and market messages shall be retained for the period required for KPI assessment, audit and settlement.

Requirement.Name: Interval aggregation
Requirement.Description: The data platform shall support aggregation and resampling to the operational and market intervals required by each pilot, including 1-minute and 15-minute periods where applicable.

Requirement.Name: Market message interoperability
Requirement.Description: Market and grid-service exchanges shall map to the formats and role definitions required by the relevant market operator, DSO, TSO or aggregator.

RequirementCategory.Name: Forecasting and optimisation
RequirementCategory.Description: Contains requirements enabling reliable predictive capabilities

Requirement.Name: PV forecasting
Requirement.Description: The platform shall produce PV generation forecasts at the time resolution and horizon required for charging, BESS and market optimisation.

Requirement.Name: Load forecasting
Requirement.Description: The platform shall forecast non-flexible and controllable site demand for the relevant planning horizon.

Requirement.Name: EV demand forecasting
Requirement.Description: The platform shall forecast EV arrival, departure, energy need and charging availability using historical or declared session information.

Requirement.Name: Constraint-aware optimisation
Requirement.Description: Optimisation shall include asset power and energy limits, grid limits, charging deadlines, reserve commitments, load constraints and permissible PV curtailment.

RequirementCategory.Name: Real-time control and performance
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements enabling near-real-time control to maintain grid compliance and track market or operational commitments

Requirement.Name: Defined control cycle
Requirement.Description: Each real-time control function shall operate at a documented cycle time appropriate to its use case and shall complete calculation and dispatch within that cycle.

Requirement.Name: Real-time grid-limit supervision
Requirement.Description: The EMS shall continuously supervise aggregate import/export against the applicable connection or circuit limit.

Requirement.Name: Activation response timing
Requirement.Description: The system shall execute DSO/TSO or market activation instructions within the mandatory response time associated with the contracted product.

Requirement.Name: Setpoint execution verification
Requirement.Description: The platform shall verify actual response after dispatch and identify partial, late or failed execution.

Requirement.Name: Control conflict resolution
Requirement.Description: When multiple objectives or commitments conflict, the system shall apply a documented precedence order that protects safety and binding obligations.

Requirement.Name: Performance logging
Requirement.Description: Control-cycle start time, decision time, dispatch time, acknowledgement and measured response shall be logged for performance assessment.

RequirementCategory.Name: Grid constraints, flexibility and resilience
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements ensuring safe operation under constrained grid conditions while providing external grid services

Requirement.Name: Upward and downward flexibility calculation
Requirement.Description: The platform shall calculate feasible upward and downward power and energy flexibility with duration, availability window and recovery requirement.

Requirement.Name: Flexibility reservation
Requirement.Description: Awarded or contracted flexibility shall be reserved in asset schedules so that it remains activatable during the committed service window.

Requirement.Name: No double commitment
Requirement.Description: The system shall prevent the same asset headroom from being committed simultaneously to incompatible services or schedules.

Requirement.Name: Flexibility delivery verification
Requirement.Description: The system shall compare requested and measured response and calculate delivered power, energy, duration and accuracy.

RequirementCategory.Name: Market, aggregator and external platform integration
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements ensuring integration into electricity and flexibility markets

Requirement.Name: Awarded schedule reception
Requirement.Description: The VPP/aggregator interface shall receive and validate accepted schedules, prices and delivery periods and make them available to the EMS.

Requirement.Name: Reserve capacity bidding
Requirement.Description: The platform shall provide upward and downward mFRR availability profiles and capacity bids for the applicable settlement intervals.

Requirement.Name: Activation-order handling
Requirement.Description: The system shall receive, authenticate, validate and execute activation orders containing direction, magnitude, start time and duration.

Requirement.Name: Settlement result exchange
Requirement.Description: The external-platform interface shall exchange delivered quantities, prices, penalties, imbalance results and remuneration components with the responsible party.

RequirementCategory.Name: Metering, verification, settlement and KPI reporting
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements providing grounds for operational control and project and market outcomes validation

Requirement.Name: Connection-point metering
Requirement.Description: The system shall measure net import/export at the relevant connection point with accuracy and interval resolution suitable for control and, where applicable, settlement.

Requirement.Name: Baseline calculation
Requirement.Description: Where service delivery is assessed against a baseline, the platform shall calculate and retain the applicable adjusted reference value and its input data.

Requirement.Name: Settlement-grade audit trail
Requirement.Description: Measurements used for financial settlement shall be immutable or tamper-evident, timestamped and traceable through all processing steps.

Requirement.Name: KPI computation
Requirement.Description: The platform shall calculate the applicable project KPIs, including PV self-consumption, peak reduction, curtailment avoidance, operating cost, flexibility potential and charging-service performance.

Requirement.Name: Delivery report
Requirement.Description: The system shall generate reports comparing requested, scheduled and actual power/energy for each flexibility or market event.

RequirementCategory.Name: Cybersecurity, privacy and access control
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements ensuring secure and privacy-preserving access to services and provide resilient operation of infrastructure

Requirement.Name: Strong authentication
Requirement.Description: Human users, devices and external systems shall authenticate before accessing telemetry, configuration, commands, bids or personal data.

Requirement.Name: Encryption in transit
Requirement.Description: All communications crossing device, site, cloud or organisational trust boundaries shall use appropriate encryption in transit.

Requirement.Name: Command integrity and anti-replay
Requirement.Description: Control commands and market activations shall be protected against unauthorised modification, duplication and replay.

RequirementCategory.Name: Safety, fault handling and recovery
RequirementCategory.Description: Group of requirements ensuring control platform never overrides asset or mobility safety constraints

Requirement.Name: Asset safety-envelope enforcement
Requirement.Description: No EMS, CSMS or market command shall exceed the validated electrical, thermal, SoC, ramp-rate or manufacturer limits of an asset.

Requirement.Name: Recovery validation
Requirement.Description: Following a fault or outage, the system shall verify communications, status, limits and metering before returning an asset to automatic control.
